items.title: Presentations and Announcements
2023 Budget Overview
notes: Presentation by D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer welcomed everyone to Council’s first budget meeting. He indicated the agenda is divided into 3 categories;

Budget Orientation/Introduction, Budget Policy Approvals and Project Pre-Approvals. D. Wilson outlined the 2023 budget pressures, including inflation, assessment growth, insurance premiums, utility and gas prices, payroll costs, and Bill 23. He noted cumulatively, the Township owns, operates and maintains assets with replacement values in excess of $1 billion dollars.

D. Wilson highlighted the state of Township assets, the asset management strategy – risk management, factors impacting levels of service, tax supported capital funding and a summary of capital investment for tax supported assets, excluding water and wastewater assets.

items.title: Consideration of Reports - Budget Introduction
2023 Budget Basics and Significant Areas Impacting the 2023 Budget
notes: & Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services &

items.title: Treasurer
notes: A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the budget process, including how the budget works, the timeline, revenue sources (property taxation, taxation assessment, assessment growth, OMPF funding, and fees and charges).
He noted the tax supported operating budget breakdown, as well as other areas impacting the 2023 budget including capital overview and water and wastewater.
A. McNabb outlined other significant items impacting the 2023 Operating Budget, including inflation, staffing costs, fuel costs, and insurance premiums and capital funding.

He responded to questions regarding the delay in the Ontario Property tax reassessment and the anticipated approach towards the implementation, the difference between reserves and reserve funds, green initiatives, process followed to collect delinquent tax accounts, water and wastewater cost recovery goals, and timing for a new development charges by-law.
Mayor Watters called a 7 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 10:40 am.

items.title: 2023 Draft Capital Budget
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2023 preliminary capital budget, including significant sources of funding, the background and purpose of dedicated capital levy and the OCIF funded bridge plan, and capital budget facts. He outlined the capital budget document layout and details of the significant capital projects, including plans and studies, parking & recreation, roads & bridges, water & wastewater, and facilities.

Mark Bradey responded to questions regarding reference numbers for older projects, developer contributions, the relationship between the strategic plan and the capital budget, OCIF funding and associated projects.
Mayor Watters called a 5 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 11:20 am.
Various staff highlighted several projects using the Centre Wellington Capital Budget Dashboard.
Tom Mulvey, Fire Chief provided an update and rationale for the purchase of a new pumper, including the timeframe for delivery and expected costs.
Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services provided an overview of the purpose for the Water/Wastewater Servicing Master Plan Study.

Rashid Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer provided an overview of the proposed external market compensation review to be conducted using select municipal comparators to determine market positioning for benchmark positions using various percentile comparisons to ensure all job descriptions and job evaluation results are current and defensible.

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the proposal to continue the parking pilot program for the 2023 season and the creation of a long term parking strategy that could include recommendations for parking requirements in both downtowns, including review of the shuttle bus, exploring parking permits, paid parking, etc. He responded to questions regarding the timing of the study to ensure alignment with active transportation initiatives and review of the enforcement

Matt Tucker, Manager of Parks and Facilities Operations provided an overview of the Victoria Park, Elora stair replacement. He responded to questions regarding the timing of the project to lessen the impact on tourists, funding received from RTO4 covering consultant fees and consultation with stakeholders such as the local kayak group.

Colin Baker with the assistance of Adam Gilmore, Manager of Engineering provided an overview of several road and bridge projects, including the Beatty Line Bridge 3N, Eighth Line West Reconstruction, Fifth Line Bridge (18 WG), Municipal Class Environmental Assessment (Structure 1-P), St. David Street N to St. Andrew St to Edinburgh Ave, Clyde Street pumping station, Dickson Drive employment land servicing, McNab Street watermain replacement, potential new well areas #3 and #7, replacement of existing trunk storm sewer, and the Municipal Operations Centre.
Dan Wilson provided an overview of the Elora Municipal Office and the Queen Street Administration Centre Retro-Fit projects due to a low inventory of administration space.

Staff responded to questions regarding the reconstruction project for 24- WG bridge, funding opportunities, rezoning and multi-use trail associated with the Operation Centre lands, odour improvements at the Clyde Street pumping station, sidewalks and traffic calming measures for McNabb Street,
Mayor Watters recessed for lunch. The meeting resumed at 1:15 pm.

items.title: OLG Funding Allocation Policy
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview, outlining the revisions to the allocations. A.

McNabb indicated staff is recommending the Arts, Culture & Heritage category be split into a category for Community Impact Grants and a category for Heritage. The anticipated funding for 2023 is as follows:

Community Impact (added to existing grant process) $108,000, Heritage $81,000. The proposed allocation provides a total of 7% OLG allocated to Community Impact Grants and Heritage combined, up from previous annual allocations of 5%.

Staff responded to questions and comments associated with the removal of the words “Arts and Culture”, the increase of the allocation to 90% to support significant projects, and provided an explanation that additional details on the Community Impact Grant and use of the allocated funds will be brought forward at a future meeting.
